standard_prerequisites.name: Hausdorff dimension and Hausdorff measure of a subset of a Euclidean space
standard_prerequisites.statement: DimH(A) is the infimum of the s for which the s-dimensional Hausdorff measure of A vanishes; a bi-Lipschitz image of A has the same dimension, and a graph of a Lipschitz function on an open subset of R^m has dimension m.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: the authors' own definition and conventions at source lines 309-331
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the invariant being computed and the tool used at the end of the proof, where the set is shown to be a 1-Lipschitz graph over a spacelike subspace of dimension n-2.

standard_prerequisites.name: Duality and affine charts in real projective space
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every point x of a convex domain boundary has a tangent hyperplane x*, the dual projective space parametrizes hyperplanes, and after choosing two boundary points x_0, x_infinity with covectors alpha_0, alpha_infinity the affine patch P(R^n) minus x_infinity^* is identified with V x R, V = x_0^* cap x_infinity^*, by (v,t) -> [v + t v_infinity + v_0].
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: the authors' own setup at source lines 1017-1023
standard_prerequisites.use: Only this elementary projective duality and the two explicit affine charts are assumed; the formula for the dual point and the dimension bound are retained obligations.

standard_prerequisites.name: Strict convexity of a C^1 function and Brouwer's invariance of domain
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a strictly convex C^1 function f one has d_u f(v-u) < f(v) - f(u) for u different from v; an injective continuous map from an open subset of R^m into R^m is open.
standard_prerequisites.use: Strict convexity supplies the strict positivity of the quadratic form on difference vectors, and invariance of domain converts injectivity of the orthogonal projection onto a spacelike subspace into the graph representation that yields the 1-Lipschitz bound.

core_obligations: Fix two distinct boundary points x_0, x_infinity with vectors v_0, v_infinity and covectors alpha_0, alpha_infinity pairing to one, identify the affine patch P(R^n) minus x_infinity^* with V x R for V = x_0^* cap x_infinity^*, and write the boundary as the graph of a C^1 strictly convex function f: V -> R (source lines 1016-1019).

Identify the dual chart and compute the dual point of (u, f(u)) as (u,f(u))* = (-d_uf, d_uf(u) - f(u)), reducing the statement to the claim that the set {(u, d_uf) : u in V} has Hausdorff dimension n-2 after transporting by the C^1 isomorphism pi (source lines 1021-1041).

Introduce the symmetric bilinear form <(u,alpha),(v,beta)> = alpha(v) + beta(u) on V x V*, note that it is non-degenerate of signature (n-2,n-2), and prove that pi(partial Omega^sym) is spacelike by computing the square of the difference vector (v-u, d_vf - d_uf) and using strict convexity of f to make it strictly positive (source lines 1043-1058).

Choose a spacelike subspace W of dimension n-2, show that the orthogonal projection of pi(partial Omega^sym) to W is injective, and use Brouwer's invariance of domain to conclude that the set is the graph of a function over an open subset of W; since the set is spacelike this graph is 1-Lipschitz with respect to the form on W and minus the form on W-perp (source lines 1060-1060).

Conclude that pi(partial Omega^sym) is a Lipschitz manifold of dimension n-2 and therefore that the symmetric boundary partial Omega^sym itself has Hausdorff dimension n-2, the dimension being preserved by the C^1 isomorphism pi (source line 1060).
proof_roadmap: Choose two distinct boundary points and the two affine charts of P(R^n) and of its dual that make the boundary a graph of a C^1 strictly convex function f.
Compute the dual point (u,f(u))* = (-d_uf, d_uf(u) - f(u)) and identify the symmetric boundary with the set {(u, d_uf)} up to the C^1 isomorphism pi.
Put the symmetric form <(u,alpha),(v,beta)> = alpha(v) + beta(u) on V x V* and verify that difference vectors of the set have strictly positive square, which is exactly strict convexity of f.
Project orthogonally onto a spacelike subspace W of dimension n-2; injectivity plus invariance of domain makes the set a graph, and spacelikeness makes that graph 1-Lipschitz.
Read off that the set is a Lipschitz manifold of dimension n-2 and transfer the dimension back through pi.
difficulty_reason: The theorem computes the Hausdorff dimension of the symmetric boundary partial Omega^sym = {(x,x*) : x in partial Omega} of a strictly convex projective domain with C^1 boundary, where the duality homeomorphism x -> x* is not C^1 unless the boundary is C^2, so the dimension of its graph is not immediate (the authors say so at source line 1014). The proof chooses two boundary points, identifies an affine patch with V x R, writes the boundary as the graph of a C^1 strictly convex function f, computes the dual point (u,f(u))* = (-d_uf, d_uf(u) - f(u)) and reduces the claim to the set {(u, d_uf)} in V x V*. The step that cannot be done routinely is the dimension bound itself: the authors introduce the symmetric bilinear form <(u,alpha),(v,beta)> = alpha(v) + beta(u) of signature (n-2,n-2), prove that difference vectors of the set have strictly positive square using d_uf(v-u) < f(v) - f(u), and then combine injectivity of the orthogonal projection onto a spacelike subspace with Brouwer's invariance of domain to exhibit the set as a 1-Lipschitz graph of dimension n-2 (source lines 1043-1060).
